Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a hermitian operator

Source: R/eigs.R
eigs.Rd

Lanczos with full reorthogonalisation, run against the operator's action. The result records what converged, what residual each pair reached, and what argument establishes the bound on the eigenvalues.

Usage

eigs(
  A,
  k,
  which = "largest",
  sigma = NULL,
  B = NULL,
  tol = 1e-10,
  maxit = NULL,
  ncv = NULL,
  v0 = NULL,
  seed = 1L,
  method = "auto",
  inner = list(),
  section = list(),
  floor_const = SOLVE_FLOOR_CONST,
  norm_control = list()
)

Arguments

A

A square hermitian `linop`. No adjoint is required.

k

How many eigenpairs.

which

Which end of the spectrum: `"largest"` or `"smallest"` by magnitude, `"largest_algebraic"` or `"smallest_algebraic"` by value. RSpectra's `"LM"`, `"SM"`, `"LA"` and `"SA"` are accepted for the same four.

sigma

A real shift. Given one, the eigenvalues nearest `sigma` are sought, by running the same recurrence on `(A - sigma I)^-1` through the package's own solvers. `which` does not apply and passing both is an error.

B

Reserved for the generalized problem `A x = lambda B x`, which is not in this version.

tol

Convergence tolerance. Every method holds each pair, measured on `A`, to the backward error `||A x - mu x|| / (||A|| ||x||)` and to the relative residual `||A x - mu x|| / (|mu| ||x||)` wherever `|mu|` is above the arithmetic floor, each plus that floor: the certificate's `backward error` and `residual` rows.

maxit

Budget of applies across all restarts, of the operator the iteration runs on: `A`, or under `sigma` the inner solve. `NULL` takes `20 n` for an `n x n` operator, twenty times what forming it column by column would cost. Hard ends of a spectrum need applies that grow with `n` at a fixed `ncv` (seven times `n` for the largest eigenvalue of the 1-D Laplacian at `n = 2000`), so the default grows with it. A run that stops improving ends before the budget does, and a run that exhausts it returns a `fail` certificate.

ncv

Subspace size per restart. Storage is `ncv` vectors. `NULL` takes the engine's default: `max(2k + 1, k + 20)` for `"lanczos"`, and PRIMME's own basis size for `"primme"`.

v0

Starting vector, or `NULL` for a seeded random one.

seed

Seed for the starting vector. The caller's random stream is restored afterwards.

method

`"auto"`, `"lanczos"` or `"primme"`. `"lanczos"` is the reference implementation in this package. `"primme"` is the PRIMME library, available when the `linop.primme` package is installed, which restarts implicitly and so keeps a basis of fixed small size. `"auto"` takes PRIMME when it is available and Lanczos otherwise; the certificate's `dispatch` records every engine considered and why. Whichever runs, the reported values are Rayleigh quotients measured on `A` and the certificate is the same.

inner

Arguments for the inner solve when `sigma` is given, such as `method` or `tol`.

section

Arguments for the truncation, when `A` is an operator on a sequence space and has no matrix: `n_start` for how much free tail the first section leaves beyond the window, and `n_max` for the widest section the search may reach. The width itself is not among them, because `eigs(finite_section(A, n))` is already how a caller fixes it.

floor_const

`c` in the arithmetic floor of the certificate.

norm_control

Arguments for the `||A||` estimate.

Value

An object of class `linop_eigen`, with `values`, `vectors` and the `certificate`. A run that exhausts its budget returns the best pairs it reached and a `fail` certificate rather than an error, and it may hold fewer than `k` of them: nothing is padded. On a sequence space it also carries the width `n` that was chosen and the `widths` that were tried.

Details

The eigenvalue reported for each pair is the Rayleigh quotient `x^H A x / (x^H x)`, measured on `A` itself. It is the value that minimises `||A x - mu x||`, so no other choice of `mu` certifies better.

`target identity` is `not_checked`, always. A small residual proves the pair is an approximate eigenpair; that it is the largest, smallest or nearest one requires an inertia count, an enclosure or a separation bound, and matrix-free there is generally none. See `vignette("certificates")`.

Examples

n <- 40
L <- linop(function(X) rbind(X[-1, , drop = FALSE], 0) +
                       rbind(0, X[-n, , drop = FALSE]) - 2 * X,
           dim = c(n, n), properties = c(hermitian = TRUE))
fit <- eigs(L, k = 3, which = "largest_algebraic")
fit$values

## on an operator with no matrix, where the width is chosen rather than given
H <- linop_jacobi(diagonal = 1)
fit <- eigs(H, k = 1, which = "largest_algebraic")
fit$n
fit$values - sqrt(5)
